newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks surge in early trade on Dow rise.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks surge in early trade on Dow rise.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks staged a strong rally in early trade on Wednesday, buoyed by an overnight surge in the Dow industrials to a record high.
The Hang Seng Index was up 277.54 points, or 1.80 percent, at 15,724.32. Turnover was HK$2.85 billion after the first half hour of trade.
"The market is following Wall Street," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
The Dow industrials surged 154.93 points, or 1.96 percent, to a record 8,061.65 on Tuesday following comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Greenspan said the Fed would raise interest rates if needed but suggested that might not happen anytime soon. Investors perceived the comments as suggesting Fed policy was on hold.
Galbraith said the interest rate environment should help the property sector, which has been under pressure due to government plans to curb rising real estate prices.

Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$0.25 to HK$73.75. The company said on Tuesday it would offer an additional 136 flats at its Vista Paradiso residential development in the New Territories following the good response to an initial 204 units offered and then another 130 units offered on Monday.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd rose HK$1.25 to HK$89.50 and New World Development Co Ltd gained HK$0.70 to HK$48.70.
"I think we will begin to see property developers start outperforming, especially with lower interest rates," said Galbraith.
Utility stocks continued their strong performance, with investors expecting more business for utility companies due to the government's plans to increase housing supply.
Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd was up HK$0.40 to HK$32.00 and China Light and Power Co Ltd added HK$0.30 to HK$44.50.
Hongkong Telecom gained HK$0.20 to HK$20.15.
"It all boils down to more houses means extended utilities," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Heavyweight HSBC Holdings Plc jumped HK$4.00 to HK$263.00.
